segments.t: Still rattled by his midnight nightmare, Denis makes the mistake of describing his dream to Senya, Fedya, and Ainura in the kitchen. While the guys tease him about having tiny hands, superstitious Ainura predicts that the dream means he will break his arm. Let's listen to their banter in Russian.
Во сне играла какая-то странная музыка.
Я смотрю на свои руки.
А они маленькие, как у ребёнка.
Денис, я не хочу тебя расстраивать.
Слушай, Денис, ты так не переживай.
Ничего очень страшного в этом нет.
Просто скоро руку сломаешь, и всё.
Спасибо, Айнура, ты меня очень утешила.
Хватит, чего вы напали на парня?
Ну, маленькие руки, и что дальше?
Ладно, друг, не переживай, дай пять!
Так, быстро разошлись все по местам!
Now let's examine how the kitchen crew reacts to Denis's dream line by line.
Во сне играла какая-то странная музыка.
'Some strange music was playing in the dream.' An indefinite feminine modifier pairs with an adjective and the nominative noun for music.
Я смотрю на свои руки.
'I look at my hands.' Denis uses the historical present to make his retelling of the nightmare more vivid.
А они маленькие, как у ребёнка.
'And they are small, like a child's.' A comparative phrase with a possessive preposition and the genitive singular of child describes his hands.
Денис, я не хочу тебя расстраивать.
'Denis, I do not want to upset you.' Senya sets up a joke using a negated verb of wishing and an imperfective infinitive.
Слушай, Денис, ты так не переживай.
'Listen, Denis, do not worry so much.' Ainura chimes in with a negated singular imperative meaning do not worry.
Ничего очень страшного в этом нет.
'There is nothing terribly bad in that.' A negative pronoun takes a genitive singular neuter adjective in an existential clause.
Просто скоро руку сломаешь, и всё.
'You will just break your arm soon, and that's all.' In Russian, one word covers both hand and arm, used here in the accusative singular.
Спасибо, Айнура, ты меня очень утешила.
'Thanks, Ainura, you really comforted me.' Denis replies sarcastically using a feminine past perfective verb meaning comforted.
Хватит, чего вы напали на парня?
'Enough, why did you jump on the guy?' The animate accusative singular of guy follows the directional preposition after a verb of attacking.
Ну, маленькие руки, и что дальше?
'So what if he has small hands, what next?' Senya pretends to defend Denis only to set up another prank with a tiny doll hand.
Ладно, друг, не переживай, дай пять!
'All right, pal, do not worry, give me five!' The colloquial idiom for a high five uses a singular imperative of giving and the numeral five.
Так, быстро разошлись все по местам!

'All right, everyone disperse to your stations quickly!' A plural past reflexive verb functions as a sharp command for the crowd to scatter. Let's hear the kitchen conversation about Denis's nightmare from start to finish.

Denis regrets telling the pranksters about his dream before Vika steps in and sends everyone back to work. Listen for the nouns meaning music, child, and circus in their dialogue. See you in the next scene.
